q: Diesel prices changed this year. Does that distort a spend-based emissions estimate?
title: Fuel price changes and spend estimates
short: Yes. If you estimate from rupees, a price rise looks like more fuel and a price cut looks like less. Convert spend to litres with the price on each invoice date, or better, use the litres printed on the invoice. Emissions follow litres, not rupees.

p: Spend-based factors assume a fixed price. When the pump price moves, the same litres produce a different rupee total and a different estimate.

ul: Use litres from the invoice where shown.
Otherwise divide spend by the pump price on that date.

example.title: Same fuel, two estimates
lines: Rs 9,00,000 at Rs 90 per litre = 10,000 L
Rs 9,00,000 at Rs 95 per litre = 9,474 L
Using 90 overstates by 526 L, about 1,410 kg CO2
